text:
Predicates:
MultipleBirth(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth with siblings.
HasSiblingsBornTogether(x) ::: x has siblings who were born together.
ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) ::: x often complains about annoying siblings.
LivesAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home.
LivesWithStrangers(x) ::: x lives with strangers.
HangsOutWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with siblings.
PlaysWithSiblings(x) ::: x plays with siblings.
BornInMultipleBirth(x) ::: x is born in a multiple birth.
QuestionedAboutSiblings(x) ::: x complains about siblings.
Uncertain(x) ::: x's status is uncertain.

Premises:
∀x (HangsOutWithSiblings(x) ∧ PlaysWithSiblings(x) → MultipleBirth(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings, then they are born in a multiple birth.
∀x (ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(x) → HasSiblingsBornTogether(x)) ::: If people complain often about siblings, then they have siblings born together.
∀x (LivesAtHome(x) → ¬LivesWithStrangers(x)) ::: If people live at home, then they do not live with strangers.
∀x (HangsOutWithSiblings(x) ∧ PlaysWithSiblings(x) → LivesAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend time with and play with siblings, then they often live at home.
LukeIsMultipleBirthAndStrangers ::: Luke either is a baby born in a multiple birth and lives with strangers, or is not a baby born in a multiple birth and does not live with strangers.

Conclusion:
¬BornInMultipleBirth(luke) ∧ ¬ComplainsOftenAboutSiblings(luke) ::: Luke is neither born in a multiple birth nor complains often about siblings.
